argument_summary: No new evidence is offered. The certification defense should be narrowed rather than treated as a clean authorization for the exposed enterprise refund workflow. The admissible record supports that the release as a whole passed aggregate readiness, had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and will launch with a 4% rollout, monitoring, and rollback. Those points support operational caution and reversibility. But the same admissible record also shows the enterprise refund workflow remains exposed, is below target on refund-policy summarization, and is not covered by an approved, workflow-specific risk acceptance. On that record, the strongest supportable position is a caveated certification posture: the packet can defend general launch readiness and required disclosure of the limitation, while conceding that the exposed use case is not cleanly policy-compliant unless it is excluded or covered by reviewed risk acceptance before launch.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is narrower than the original defense. It says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. It also says rollback, dashboards, or a small initial percentage do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. On the current admissible evidence, disclosure is still required, but disclosure alone does not satisfy the policy predicate for the exposed enterprise refund workflow. Aggregate readiness and public governance guidance can support a risk-weighted narrative, but they do not replace the internal requirement for exclusion or approved risk acceptance.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not the only proportionate response if the record is narrowed to caveated rather than clean compliance. The rollout and monitoring evidence materially reduce operational risk and support avoiding an overbroad noncompliance conclusion for the release as a whole, even though they do not cure the policy gap for the exposed workflow.
concessions: The enterprise refund workflow remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
That workflow is below target on refund-policy summarization.
The draft risk acceptance is unapproved and does not address the enterprise refund workflow exposure.
Aggregate readiness, limited rollout, rollback capability, and monitoring are not sufficient by themselves for the exposed use case under the stated policy.
General public AI governance materials provide background support only and do not override the internal policy threshold.
